title: responses-adapter: propagate determinism/seed headers and structured-output annotations
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: The OpenAI Responses variants that customers adopt increasingly rely on explicit determinism/seed directives and lightweight structured-output annotations passed through the HTTP layer. Without preserving those hints across our OpenAI-compat adapter we observed divergences between direct upstream behavior and Redwood-hosted responses in customer compatibility testing (see ENG-4821). This PR implements two coordinated changes in the adapter and runtime surface to improve compatibility and reduce customer surprises: 1) deterministic/seed propagation: accept and translate OpenAI-style determinism flags (seed, deterministic, x-seed) present as either JSON fields in the Responses body or as HTTP headers, and persist them through the routing, reassembly, and streaming layers so that streaming reassembly uses the same determinism hint used by the model selection logic; 2) structured-output annotations: accept structured output schema hints (openai_schema, schema_hint, or x-output-schema) and surface them to the structured-output postprocessor and the tool-call router. Implementation summary: - HTTP adapter: new header handling for X-OpenAI-Seed, X-OpenAI-Deterministic and X-OpenAI-Output-Schema; these are normalized to internal headers X-Redwood-Seed and X-Redwood-Output-Schema during internal RPCs so that downstream components see a consistent key. - Payload parsing: Responses-compatible body parsing now reads top-level "determinism" and "seed" keys in addition to existing generation params and merges them with header values (headers take precedence). - Streaming reassembly: streaming reassembly now attaches a deterministic-context token to each stream chunk and includes seed metadata in the final reassembly envelope so consumers and logs can assert determinism and replay. This prevents a class of flaky stream reorder bugs seen during canary. - Tool/function calling: the toolcall envelope now carries the propagated schema hint on the function metadata so third-party tool runners can perform schema-aware validation/dispatch. - Backwards compatibility: adapter will ignore unknown header keys and continues to accept legacy openai-style body shapes; a compatibility shim maps older "seed_hint" fields to the new internal header where detected. - Tests and validations: unit tests for adapter parsing, integration tests exercising streaming reassembly with seeded responses, and an end-to-end canary against a mocked OpenAI-responses backend were added. Checklist: - [x] Add header normalization in adapter layer - [x] Merge seed into routing decisions (with tests) - [x] Attach seed/annotations to streaming reassembly envelope - [x] Surface schema hint to toolcall metadata - [x] Add integration tests and canary job - [x] Update docs/compat notes (short note in docs site) Related: ENG-4821 (compat issues during customer test runs), ENG-4835 (structured output rollout plan). Breaking change: none; feature is opt-in via header/body keys. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a config flag responses.adapter.enable_seed_passthrough (default off). We enabled the flag in the dedicated canary namespaces and verified downstream regression metrics before merging.

review_thread: Ethan Park (reviewer): Can you confirm headers take precedence over body-level seed when both are present? The compatibility matrix in ENG-4821 assumes header-first behavior.
Maya Chen (author): Yes — updated adapter/parse.go: headers override body keys. Added explicit unit tests to cover both orders.
Priya Nair (reviewer): Suggest adding a short-lived metric that counts how often seed is provided via header vs body so we can monitor usage post-rollout.
Maya Chen (author): Added seed_source metric and emitted tags (header|body|none); seen in canary results. PTAL.
Luca Romano (approver): Integration looks good. I ran the canary against the mocked backend and confirmed identical token stream orders with seed set. Approving for merge.

release_notes: Adapter: preserve and propagate Responses determinism/seed directives and structured-output hints. Opt-in via responses.adapter.enable_seed_passthrough; enables more reliable compatibility with OpenAI Responses variants and allows schema-aware tool dispatch.
